intro: Some words from the Qur'an are said every day. Muslims say them before a meal. They say them when they meet a friend. In this unit you will learn what these words mean. You may hear them at school.
The Qur'an also tells stories. Some are about a boat, a big fish and a tiny ant. Many of these people are in the Bible too. You will learn their Arabic names. You will learn their English names.
By the end, you will know four everyday words and six stories. You will be able to say, "Muslims believe this," and "The Qur'an tells this story."
bigQuestion: What words and stories from the Qur'an are part of a Muslim child's every day?

timeline.t: Amira wakes up and says As-salamu alaykum, peace be upon you, to her grandmother
Before the first bite, she says Bismillah, in the name of God
When the school bus starts to move, she says Bismillah for the trip
In class, she hears a story about Noah and a boat; the Qur'an calls him Nuh
Yusuf sits with her and whispers Bismillah before he eats
Yusuf says Alhamdulillah, thanks be to God, because he is full
A friend sneezes, and Amira says Alhamdulillah with a smile
Amira says a kind word to her mother, as the Qur'an says to do
The family shares food and says Bismillah together
Grandfather tells the story of the tiny ant who warned her friends

words.d: the words "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful"; many Muslims say them before starting something
an Arabic word that means "thanks be to God" or "praise be to God"
the Arabic word for God
a greeting that means "peace be upon you"
a person who brings a message from God, as Muslims believe
the Arabic name for Noah; the Qur'an says he built a big boat
the Arabic name for Moses; the prophet named most often in the Qur'an
the square building in Mecca that the Qur'an says Ibrahim and Ismail built

test.why: Bismillah means "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."

test.q: When do many Muslims say Bismillah?
choices: Before they start something, like a meal
test.why: Many Muslims say Bismillah before starting something, like eating, homework or a trip.
Alhamdulillah means "thanks be to God" or "praise be to God."

test.q: What is the Arabic word for God?
test.why: Allah is the Arabic word for God. A surah is a chapter, and the Kaaba is a building.
As-salamu alaykum is a greeting that means "peace be upon you."

test.q: What does the Qur'an say about parents?
choices: Be kind to them and speak gently
test.why: The Qur'an (17:23) says to be kind to parents and speak to them with respect.

test.q: Who built a big boat before a flood, as the Qur'an tells it?
test.why: The Qur'an says Nuh (Noah) built the ark. Yunus was swallowed by a fish, and Sulayman heard the ant.

test.q: What happened to baby Musa, as the Qur'an tells it?
choices: His mother put him in a basket on the river
test.why: The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in the river, and Pharaoh's wife found him.

test.q: Who is Isa, as Muslims believe?
choices: A prophet, the son of Maryam
test.why: Muslims believe Isa (Jesus) was a prophet born to Maryam (Mary).

test.q: Who smiled when a tiny ant warned her friends?
test.why: The Qur'an (27:19) says Sulayman (Solomon) smiled at the ant's words and thanked God.

write.prompt: Pick one story from this unit: Nuh's boat, Yunus and the fish, Musa in the basket, or the ant. Draw or write what happens. Tell where it is in the Qur'an (like surah 27, The Ant). Then tell one thing Muslims believe about the person in the story.
tips: Start with "The Qur'an tells this story."
Use the Arabic name and the English name, like Nuh (Noah).
Say "Muslims believe" when you tell what Muslims believe.
If the Bible tells the story too, you can say so.

title: Words Muslims Say Every Day

chapters.title: Bismillah and Alhamdulillah
chapters.bigQuestion: What words from the Qur'an do Muslims say every day, and what do they mean?

story.title: Four Words Before Lunch
story.kicker: Yusuf opens his lunch box, and before the first bite, he whispers something.
paragraphs: It is lunchtime at school. Yusuf sits down with his friend Maya. He opens his lunch box. There is rice, chicken and a little box of grapes. Maya is already eating her sandwich.
Yusuf holds his spoon still for a moment. He whispers four soft words. Then he starts to eat. Maya looks up. "What did you say?" she asks. "I said Bismillah," Yusuf tells her.

"It means, In the name of God," Yusuf says. "My family says it before we eat. We say it before a trip too. It is from the Qur'an." Maya nods. "My grandma says a little prayer before dinner," she says.
When Yusuf finishes, he says one more word. "Alhamdulillah." Maya smiles. "What does that one mean?" Yusuf says, "Thanks be to God. I say it when I am done, because I am full and happy."
story.think: Yusuf says special words before and after he eats. Does your family say any special words at mealtime? What are they?

lessons.title: The Bismillah
lessons.mainIdea: The Bismillah is a line from the Qur'an that means "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."
reading: Almost every *surah* in the Qur'an begins with the same line. Muslims call this line the *Bismillah*. It is the very first line of the whole book.
The Bismillah says, "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." Gracious means kind. Merciful means forgiving. Muslims believe these are two names of God.
In Arabic, the Bismillah is only four words. Many Muslim children learn it very young. Often it is the first line of the Qur'an they know.

words.d: the line that begins almost every surah; it means "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful"
a chapter of the Qur'an; there are 114 of them

look.title: The First Line of the Qur'an
look.text: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
look.cite: Qur'an 1:1, Surah Al-Fatiha (The Opening), Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: This translator uses the word "Beneficent." That is an old word for kind. What two things does this line say about God, as Muslims believe?

check.q: What does the Bismillah mean?
choices: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
check.why: The Bismillah means "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." Thanks and peace are other words.

check.q: Where does the Bismillah come in the Qur'an?
choices: At the start of almost every surah
In the middle of every page
check.why: Almost every surah begins with the Bismillah. It is also the first line of the whole book.

check.q: How many Arabic words are in the Bismillah?
check.why: In Arabic the Bismillah is four words. That is why it is easy for children to learn.

lessons.title: When Muslims Say Bismillah
lessons.mainIdea: Many Muslims say Bismillah before they start something, like eating, working or going on a trip.
reading: Yusuf said *Bismillah* before he ate. Many Muslims say it before a meal. It is a way of starting with God's name. Some families say it out loud. Some whisper it.
Muslims say Bismillah at other times too. Some say it before they start homework. Some say it before they get in the car for a trip. Some say it before a game.
Muslims believe that saying God's name first makes a good beginning. You might hear a friend say it at lunch. Now you will know what it means.

words.d: the words "In the name of God"; many Muslims say them before starting something

look.title: A Day With Bismillah
look.text: Look at Amira's day. She says Bismillah before breakfast. She says it before she opens her reading book. She says it when the school bus starts to move. She says it before she kicks the ball at recess.
look.prompt: What do all the times Amira says Bismillah have in common? What is she about to do each time?

check.q: When do many Muslims say Bismillah?
choices: Before they start something, like eating
check.why: Many Muslims say Bismillah before they start something, like a meal, homework or a trip.

check.q: Why do Muslims say Bismillah first, as they believe?
choices: Because it is a loud word
Because the teacher tells them to
Because starting with God's name makes a good beginning
check.why: Muslims believe that starting with God's name makes a good beginning. That is their reason.

check.q: Yusuf whispers Bismillah before lunch. What is he doing?
choices: Starting his meal with God's name
check.why: Yusuf is starting his meal with God's name. That is what the Bismillah is for.

lessons.title: Alhamdulillah, Thanks Be to God
lessons.mainIdea: Alhamdulillah means "thanks be to God" or "praise be to God," and it is the second line of the Qur'an.
reading: After lunch, Yusuf said *Alhamdulillah*. This word means "thanks be to God." It can also mean "praise be to God." Praise means saying that someone is good.
Alhamdulillah is in the Qur'an. It is the second line of the first surah, Al-Fatiha. The line says, "Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds."
Muslims say Alhamdulillah when something good happens. They say it after a meal. They say it when they feel well. Some say it even after a sneeze!

words.d: an Arabic word that means "thanks be to God" or "praise be to God"
saying that someone is good

look.title: The Second Line
look.text: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. (Muslims read this as a line of thanks to God, who they believe made and cares for everything.)
look.cite: Qur'an 1:2, Surah Al-Fatiha (The Opening), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Yusuf says Alhamdulillah after he eats. How is his word like this line of the Qur'an?

check.q: What does Alhamdulillah mean?
check.why: Alhamdulillah means "thanks be to God" or "praise be to God." Bismillah means "in the name of God."

check.q: When might a Muslim say Alhamdulillah?
choices: When something bad is about to start
When something good happens, like finishing a meal
check.why: Muslims say Alhamdulillah as thanks, when something good happens. Yusuf said it after his meal.

check.q: Where is Alhamdulillah found in the Qur'an?
choices: In the second line of Al-Fatiha
It is not in the Qur'an
check.why: The second line of Al-Fatiha, the first surah, begins "Praise be to God."

lessons.title: Allah Means God
lessons.mainIdea: Allah is the Arabic word for God; Muslims believe there is only one God.
reading: You heard the word *Allah* inside Bismillah and Alhamdulillah. Allah is the *Arabic* word for God. Arabic is the language of the Qur'an.
Muslims believe there is only one God. When Muslims speak English, many still say Allah. Others say God. Both words mean the same thing to them.
Some Christians who speak Arabic also say Allah when they mean God. It is a word, like "Dios" in Spanish. Different languages have different words for God.

words.d: the Arabic word for God
the language the Qur'an is written in

look.title: One Word, Many Languages
look.text: Look at three words on a board. In English: God. In Spanish: Dios. In Arabic: Allah. Three friends read them. One says, "That is my word." Another says, "That is mine." The third says, "That is mine."
look.prompt: The three friends use different words. What is the same about what the words mean?

check.q: What does the word Allah mean?
check.why: Allah is the Arabic word for God. It is not a person or a chapter.

check.q: How many gods do Muslims believe there are?
check.why: Muslims believe there is only one God. This is a key belief in Islam.

check.q: What language is the Qur'an written in?
check.why: The Qur'an is written in Arabic. Allah is the Arabic word for God.

lessons.title: Peace Be Upon You
lessons.mainIdea: As-salamu alaykum is a greeting that means "peace be upon you," and the answer is "and upon you, peace."
reading: When Muslims meet, they often say *As-salamu alaykum*. It means "peace be upon you." It is a way to say hello. It is also a kind wish.
The answer is "Wa alaykum as-salam." That means "and upon you, peace." So both people wish each other *peace*. The Qur'an tells people to answer a greeting with one as good or better.
You might hear this greeting at school. Muslim families in Chicago say it every day. Now you know what it means. You know how to answer, too.

words.d: a greeting that means "peace be upon you"
calm and safety; no fighting

look.title: Answer a Greeting Kindly
look.text: The Qur'an says that when someone greets you, you should greet them back with a better greeting, or at least the same one.
look.cite: Qur'an 4:86, Surah An-Nisa (The Women), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: A friend says "peace be upon you." What could you say back that is just as kind?

check.q: What does As-salamu alaykum mean?
check.why: As-salamu alaykum means "peace be upon you." It is a greeting.

check.q: What is the answer to As-salamu alaykum?
choices: Wa alaykum as-salam, and upon you, peace
check.why: The answer is "Wa alaykum as-salam," which means "and upon you, peace."

check.q: What does the Qur'an say to do when someone greets you?
choices: Greet them back as kindly or more kindly
check.why: The Qur'an (4:86) says to answer a greeting with one as good or better.

sections.title: What the Qur'an Says to Do

lessons.title: Be Kind to Parents
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says to be kind to your parents and to speak to them gently.
reading: The Qur'an has words about how to treat people. It says many times to be kind to your *parents*. Parents are your mother and father.
One surah talks about parents who are old. It says not to say even a small unkind word to them. It says to speak to them with *respect*. Respect means treating someone as important.
Muslims read these lines and try to follow them. Many other families teach the same thing. Being kind to parents is a rule that many people share.

words.d: a person's mother and father
treating someone as important; being polite to them

look.title: Gentle Words for Parents
look.text: The Qur'an says to be kind to your parents. If one or both of them grow old with you, do not say even a small unkind word to them. Speak to them with respect.
look.cite: Qur'an 17:23, Surah Al-Isra (The Night Journey), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: What is one kind thing you could say to a parent or a grandparent today?

check.q: What does the Qur'an say about parents?
choices: Ignore them when they are old
Be kind to them and speak gently
check.why: The Qur'an (17:23) says to be kind to parents and to speak to them with respect.

check.q: What does respect mean?
check.why: Respect means treating someone as important and being polite to them.

check.q: Who reads these lines and tries to follow them?
check.why: Muslims read the Qur'an and try to follow what it says. Many other families teach the same rule.

lessons.title: Share and Tell the Truth
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says to share with people who need help and to say what is true.
reading: The Qur'an says to *share*. It says to give food and money to people who are poor. It says to help *orphans*. An orphan is a child whose parents have died.
The Qur'an also says to tell the truth. One line tells people to speak words that are straight and true. Muslims believe lying is wrong.
You already know some of these rules. Share. Help. Tell the truth. The Qur'an says them in Arabic. Many books and families say them too.

words.d: to give part of what you have to someone else
a child whose parents have died

look.title: Two Children, One Cookie
look.text: Look at two children at a table. One has a cookie. The other has none. The first child breaks the cookie in half and gives one half away. Then the teacher asks, "Who ate the last cookie?" The child says, "I did. I shared it."
look.prompt: Which two things that the Qur'an says to do did this child do?

check.q: What is an orphan?
choices: A child whose parents have died
check.why: An orphan is a child whose parents have died. The Qur'an says to help orphans.

check.q: What does the Qur'an say about words?
check.why: The Qur'an (33:70) tells people to speak words that are straight and true.

check.q: Who does the Qur'an say to share with?
choices: People who are poor and orphans
check.why: The Qur'an says to give to the poor and to help orphans (2:177, 107:1-3).

review.why: Bismillah means "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."
Alhamdulillah means "thanks be to God" or "praise be to God."
Allah is the Arabic word for God. Arabic is the language of the Qur'an.

review.q: A friend says As-salamu alaykum. What should you say back?
review.why: The answer is "Wa alaykum as-salam," which means "and upon you, peace."

review.q: Which line begins almost every surah?
review.why: Almost every surah begins with the Bismillah. It is also the first line of the whole Qur'an.

review.q: The Qur'an says to be kind to parents, share and tell the truth. Who tries to follow these words?
review.why: Muslims read the Qur'an and try to follow it. Many other families teach the same things.

chapters.title: Stories the Qur'an Tells
chapters.bigQuestion: What stories does the Qur'an tell, and which ones do other families know too?

story.title: The Ant Who Warned Her Friends
story.kicker: A tiny ant sees a king's army coming and calls out to all the other ants.
paragraphs: The Qur'an tells a story about a king named Sulayman. In English, his name is Solomon. Muslims believe he was a prophet. A prophet brings a message from God. The Qur'an says Sulayman could understand birds and other animals.
One day, Sulayman marched with his army. There were people, and there were jinn, and there were birds. The ground shook with their steps. They came to a valley where many ants lived.
A tiny ant looked up. She saw the army coming closer. She called out to all the other ants. "Go into your homes! Hurry! Sulayman and his army are coming. They might step on you and not even know it."
Sulayman heard the ant. The Qur'an says he smiled. He thanked God for letting him understand her words. And the ants hurried home, safe. This story is in a surah called The Ant.
story.think: The ant was tiny, but she helped her friends. What did she do that was brave or kind?

lessons.title: Nuh and the Big Boat
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an tells about Nuh (Noah), who built a big boat and was saved from a flood.
reading: The Qur'an tells a story about *Nuh*. In English, his name is Noah. Muslims believe Nuh was a *prophet*, a person who brings a message from God. He told people to worship one God.
The Qur'an says most people did not listen. So God told Nuh to build a big boat, an ark. Then rain came, and water rose. Nuh, his family and the animals were safe on the boat.
The Bible tells a story about Noah too. The two books tell it in different ways. But many families know a story about Noah and a boat. Muslim, Jewish and Christian families all do.

words.d: the Arabic name for Noah; the Qur'an says he built a big boat
a person who brings a message from God, as Muslims believe

look.title: The Water Goes Down
look.text: The Qur'an says that after the flood, the earth was told to swallow its water. The sky was told to stop raining. The water went down, and the boat came to rest on a mountain.
look.cite: Qur'an 11:44, Surah Hud, paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Where did the boat stop when the water went down?

check.q: What is the English name for Nuh?
check.why: Nuh is the Arabic name for Noah. Yunus is Jonah and Musa is Moses.

check.q: What did Nuh build, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an says God told Nuh to build an ark, a big boat, before the flood.

check.q: Which other book tells a story about Noah and a boat?
check.why: The Bible also tells about Noah and the ark. The two books tell it in different ways.

lessons.title: Yunus and the Big Fish
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an tells about Yunus (Jonah), who was swallowed by a big fish and then set safe on land.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Yunus*. In English, his name is Jonah. The Qur'an says Yunus left his people and got on a ship. Then he was thrown into the sea.
A big fish swallowed him. Inside the dark fish, Yunus called out to God. He said he was sorry. The Qur'an says God heard him, and the fish put him on the shore.
There is a surah named Yunus. The Bible tells about Jonah and a big fish too. Many children know this story from home. Some know it from a book or a song.

words.d: the Arabic name for Jonah; the Qur'an says a big fish swallowed him
the land at the edge of the sea

look.title: Inside the Dark Fish
look.text: Look at Yunus inside the fish. It is dark. It is quiet. He cannot see the sky or the sea. He is all alone. He closes his eyes and calls out to God. Then, the Qur'an says, the fish sets him on the shore, and a plant grows to give him shade.
look.prompt: What did Yunus do when he was in the dark? What happened next?

check.q: What swallowed Yunus, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an says a big fish swallowed Yunus. The Bible says a great fish swallowed Jonah.

check.q: What did Yunus do inside the fish?
choices: He sang a song about ants
check.why: The Qur'an says Yunus called out to God in the dark and said he was sorry (21:87).

check.q: What is the English name for Yunus?
check.why: Yunus is the Arabic name for Jonah. Nuh is Noah and Yusuf is Joseph.

lessons.title: Musa in the River
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says Musa's (Moses's) mother put him in a basket on the river, and he was found and kept safe.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Musa*. In English, his name is Moses. When Musa was a baby, a king called *Pharaoh* was hurting the baby boys of Musa's people.
The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in a basket on the river. Pharaoh's wife found him. She loved him and kept him. Musa's sister watched and helped bring him back to his mother to be fed.
Musa is named more times in the Qur'an than any other prophet. The Bible tells the basket story too. Many families know the baby in the basket.

words.d: the Arabic name for Moses; the prophet named most often in the Qur'an
the king of Egypt in the story of Musa

look.title: A Mother's Promise
look.text: The Qur'an says God told Musa's mother to feed her baby, and if she was afraid, to put him in the river and not to fear. She was told that her baby would come back to her.
look.cite: Qur'an 28:7, Surah Al-Qasas (The Story), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Musa's mother was afraid. What was she told would happen to her baby?

check.q: Where did Musa's mother put him, as the Qur'an tells it?
choices: In a basket on the river
check.why: The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in the river, and Pharaoh's wife found him (28:7-9).

check.q: Who found baby Musa?
check.why: The Qur'an says Pharaoh's wife found the baby and wanted to keep him.

check.q: Which prophet is named most often in the Qur'an?
check.why: Musa (Moses) is named more times in the Qur'an than any other prophet.

lessons.title: Musa at the Sea
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says the sea opened for Musa and his people, and they walked across to safety.
reading: Musa grew up. Muslims believe God sent him as a prophet. The Qur'an says Musa told *Pharaoh* to let his people go free. Pharaoh said no.
Musa led his people away. Pharaoh's army chased them. They came to the sea. The Qur'an says God told Musa to strike the sea with his stick. The water split, and each side stood up like a mountain.
Musa's people walked across on dry ground. They were safe. The Bible tells about the sea opening too. It is one of the most famous stories in both books.

words.d: the king who would not let Musa's people go free
to break or open into parts

look.title: Walls of Water
look.text: Look at Musa's people at the edge of the sea. Behind them, the army is coming. In front of them, the water is wide. Musa strikes the water with his stick. The Qur'an says the sea splits open. Water stands up on the left like a mountain. Water stands up on the right like a mountain. A dry path runs between them.
look.prompt: Which way should the people walk now? How do you think they felt?

check.q: What did Musa do at the sea, as the Qur'an tells it?
choices: He struck the sea with his stick
check.why: The Qur'an (26:63) says God told Musa to strike the sea with his stick, and it split.

check.q: What did each side of the water look like?
check.why: The Qur'an says each part of the water stood up like a great mountain.

check.q: Who was chasing Musa's people?
check.why: Pharaoh's army chased Musa's people to the sea. Sulayman's army is in the story of the ant.

lessons.title: Ibrahim and Ismail Build the Kaaba
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son Ismail built the Kaaba, the square building in Mecca.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Ibrahim*. In English, his name is Abraham. Muslims believe he was a prophet who worshiped one God. Jews and Christians tell about Abraham too.
The Qur'an says Ibrahim and his son *Ismail* built the *Kaaba*. The Kaaba is a square building in Mecca. As they built, they prayed. They asked God to accept their work.
Today Muslims face the Kaaba when they pray. Many travel to Mecca to see it. When they do, many think of Ibrahim and Ismail.

words.d: the Arabic name for Abraham; the Qur'an says he built the Kaaba with his son
the Arabic name for Ishmael, Ibrahim's son
the square building in Mecca that Muslims face when they pray

look.title: Raising the Walls
look.text: The Qur'an says that Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, the Kaaba. As they worked, they prayed, "Our Lord, accept this from us."
look.cite: Qur'an 2:127, Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: Who built the Kaaba, as the Qur'an tells it? What did they say while they built?

check.q: What is the English name for Ibrahim?
check.why: Ibrahim is the Arabic name for Abraham. Jews and Christians tell about Abraham too.

check.q: What did Ibrahim and Ismail build, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an (2:127) says Ibrahim and Ismail raised the walls of the Kaaba in Mecca.

check.q: What do Muslims do with the Kaaba today?
choices: They face it when they pray
They sail it on the sea
check.why: Muslims all over the world face the Kaaba when they pray. Many travel to Mecca to see it.

lessons.title: Maryam and Baby Isa
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an tells about Maryam (Mary) and her baby Isa (Jesus), and a whole surah is named for Maryam.
reading: The Qur'an tells about *Maryam*. In English, her name is Mary. One whole surah has her name. Muslims believe an angel told her she would have a baby boy.
The Qur'an says her baby was *Isa*. In English, his name is Jesus. The Qur'an says Maryam rested under a palm tree. Fresh dates fell for her to eat.
Muslims believe Isa was a prophet. They believe he healed people and taught them. Christians tell about Mary and Jesus too. They believe some different things about him. Both books honor Maryam.

words.d: the Arabic name for Mary; a surah of the Qur'an is named for her
the Arabic name for Jesus; Muslims believe he was a prophet

look.title: Under the Palm Tree
look.text: Look at Maryam sitting under a tall palm tree. She is tired and alone. The Qur'an says a voice told her not to be sad. It told her to shake the tree, and ripe dates fell down for her. A little stream ran by her feet.
look.prompt: What did Maryam get from the tree and the stream? Why do you think the Qur'an tells this part?

check.q: What is the English name for Maryam?
check.why: Maryam is the Arabic name for Mary. A surah of the Qur'an is named for her.

check.q: Who is Isa, as Muslims believe?
choices: A prophet, the son of Maryam
check.why: Muslims believe Isa (Jesus) was a prophet, born to Maryam. Christians believe some different things about him.

check.q: What fell from the palm tree for Maryam, as the Qur'an tells it?
check.why: The Qur'an (19:25) says ripe dates fell from the palm tree for Maryam.

sections.title: The Ant and Stories We Share

lessons.title: Sulayman and the Ant
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an says an ant warned the other ants about Sulayman's (Solomon's) army, and Sulayman smiled at her words.
reading: You read the story of the ant at the start of this chapter. The king was *Sulayman*. In English, his name is Solomon. The Qur'an says he understood the speech of birds and animals.
The ant told her friends to hurry into their homes. Sulayman heard her and *smiled*. Then he thanked God. The Qur'an says he asked to be a person who does good.
This story is in the surah called The Ant, surah 27. The Bible tells about King Solomon too, but not about the ant. That part is in the Qur'an.

words.d: the Arabic name for Solomon; the Qur'an says he understood the speech of animals
made a happy face; Sulayman smiled at the ant's words

look.title: What the Ant Said
look.text: The Qur'an says an ant called out, "Ants, go into your homes, so that Sulayman and his army do not crush you without knowing it." Sulayman smiled at her words and thanked God.
look.cite: Qur'an 27:18-19, Surah An-Naml (The Ant), paraphrased in simple words from Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran, 1930
look.prompt: The ant says the army would not know it stepped on the ants. Why does that matter in her warning?

check.q: What is the English name for Sulayman?
check.why: Sulayman is the Arabic name for Solomon. The Qur'an says he was a king and a prophet.

check.q: What did Sulayman do when he heard the ant?
check.why: The Qur'an (27:19) says Sulayman smiled at the ant's words and thanked God.

check.q: Which surah tells the story of the ant?
check.why: The story of the ant is in surah 27, which is named The Ant (An-Naml).

lessons.title: Stories Many Families Share
lessons.mainIdea: Many stories in the Qur'an are about people the Bible tells about too, so many families share them.
reading: The Qur'an tells about Nuh, Yunus, Musa and Maryam. The *Bible* tells about Noah, Jonah, Moses and Mary. These are the same people. They have different names in each book.
The two books do not tell the stories the same way. Some parts are alike. Some parts are different. Muslims, Jews and Christians each read their own book.
Some surahs are named for these people. When you hear a story about a boat, a big fish or a basket, you can say, "The Qur'an tells that story. The Bible tells it too."

words.d: the holy book of Christians; Jews share its first part, the Hebrew Bible

look.title: Surahs Named for People in Stories
look.cite: The Qur'an, surah names and numbers in the standard order of the 114 surahs
look.prompt: Which of these surahs comes first in the Qur'an? Which comes last?

check.q: Which two books tell stories about Noah, Moses and Mary?
check.why: The Qur'an and the Bible both tell about these people. They use different names and tell the stories in different ways.

check.q: Musa is the Arabic name for which person in the Bible?
check.why: Musa is Moses. Nuh is Noah and Sulayman is Solomon.

check.q: Do the Qur'an and the Bible tell the stories in the same way?
choices: No, some parts are alike and some are different
Yes, every word is the same
No, the Bible has no stories
check.why: The two books share people and stories, but they tell them differently. Each faith reads its own book.

review.q: Who built a big boat, as the Qur'an tells it?
review.why: The Qur'an says Nuh (Noah) built the ark before the flood.
The Qur'an says a big fish swallowed Yunus (Jonah), and then he was set on the shore.

choices: In a basket on the river
review.why: The Qur'an says Musa's mother put him in the river, and Pharaoh's wife found him.

review.q: Who built the Kaaba with his son Ismail, as the Qur'an tells it?
review.why: The Qur'an (2:127) says Ibrahim (Abraham) and Ismail raised the walls of the Kaaba.

review.q: A whole surah is named for which woman?
review.why: Surah 19 is named Maryam (Mary). It tells about her and her baby Isa.

review.q: Who smiled at the words of a tiny ant?
review.why: The Qur'an (27:19) says Sulayman (Solomon) smiled when he heard the ant warn her friends.
